title: Lamellar: A Rust-based Asynchronous Tasking and PGAS Runtime for High Performance Computing
problem: Legacy HPC languages like C and C++ require developers to manually guarantee memory safety, leading to potential errors that waste execution time or produce incorrect results. The technical challenge is developing a high-performance HPC runtime that provides memory safety guarantees while maintaining performance comparable to unsafe languages.
motivation: Memory safety is critical for both cybersecurity and HPC correctness, as emphasized by government directives calling for adoption of memory-safe programming languages to reduce attack surfaces.
method: Lamellar implements an asynchronous tasking and PGAS (Partitioned Global Address Space) runtime written in Rust, providing network interfaces and safe high-level abstractions including distributed LamellarArrays and Active Messages. End-users develop entirely safe Rust code while unsafe operations are confined to rigorously tested runtime code blocks. Performance is validated against C, C++, and Chapel implementations on the BALE kernel suite.
key_novelty: A Rust-based PGAS runtime that achieves memory safety guarantees through language semantics while maintaining performance parity with unsafe C/C++ and Chapel implementations.
contributions: A complete asynchronous tasking and PGAS runtime system implemented in Rust with compile-time safety guarantees
High-level distributed memory abstractions (LamellarArrays, Active Messages) enabling safe data parallelism
Comparable performance to established HPC runtimes (C, C++, Chapel) despite memory safety constraints
Demonstration that unsafe code can be confined to rigorously tested runtime components while applications remain fully safe

metrics.other: Memory safety achieved with unsafe code limited to runtime

limitations: Specific performance overheads, scalability limits at different system sizes, and detailed comparison trade-offs not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Memory-safe HPC runtime with PGAS model
